transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (AuroraMed CTO), Ethan Li (AuroraMed ML), Sofia Martinez (AuroraMed Security)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery on p95 and throughput; focus on streaming latency for clinical summarization in the EHR, concurrency expectations, and which hosting mode will meet SLOs while keeping cost predictable.

00:00 Laura Chen (AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Laura, AE here at Redwood. Miguel is our SE, he'll handle the benchmarking details.
00:18 Miguel Ortega (SE): Hi all. Quick agenda: understand your p95 targets and concurrency, capture sample prompts, agree on benchmark plan.
00:28 Dr. Priya Rao (CTO): Thanks. For background: we are building a near-real-time clinical note summarizer that streams interim summaries back to providers as they type. Our target p95 for the end-to-end streaming response (first token appear) is ~350ms at concurrencies of 30 to 80 in peak windows. Does that make sense?
01:05 Miguel Ortega (SE): Clarifying: p95 350ms for first-token streaming latency, or full completion? Those are different.
01:12 Dr. Priya Rao: First-token. We can accept higher tail for full completions. First-token is critical because UIs expect the spinner to show immediate text.
01:25 Laura Chen: Good, that lines up with other healthcare customers. Ethan, what's your typical request size and token rates?
01:34 Ethan Li (ML): Typical context is ~1,000 tokens (patient notes + recent history), prompts produce ~80 to 250 output tokens. Peak qps is around 40 sustained, spikes to 120 for short bursts during shift changes.
01:52 Miguel Ortega: Great — so we need to test for sustained concurrency 40 and bursts to 120. Also streaming workload means we should measure tokens/sec and initial token latency separately. Our baseline guidance: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value, Dedicated gives more predictable p95 and better isolation, Private adds network hops and customer-managed infra which can add ~30-120ms depending on VPC topology.
02:20 Sofia Martinez (Security): On security: we require SOC2, SSO via SAML, and KMS integration for keys. Also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Any gotchas?
02:33 Laura Chen: We have SOC2 reports and KMS integrations; we also support forwarding audit logs and can do VPC peering for private installs. We'll send the security packet after the call.
02:45 Dr. Priya Rao: On cost, we need a sense of tokens/sec unit economics — how much does streaming with p95 <350 cost vs relaxing to 600ms?
02:56 Miguel Ortega: Good question — cost delta is mostly due to required capacity headroom. For Dedicated you size GPU pool for peak concurrency; for Hosted you pay per usage but might see higher variance. We can run a microbenchmark to quantify tokens/sec and cost per 1k output tokens across modes.
03:20 Ethan Li: What's your approach to token/sec benchmarks? We care about realistic client patterns — prefix cache, repeated prompts, and long context.
03:30 Miguel Ortega: We'll run three phases: 1) synthetic microbench: fixed prompt, measure tokens/sec and first-token p95 at concurrency 1/10/50/200; 2) realistic replay: replay your 200 sample prompts with actual contexts, measure streaming inter-token latency and aggregate p95; 3) stability: 1 hour sustained with concurrency ~40 to assess tail and memory/kv cache behavior. We'll include KV/prefix cache enabled/disabled to show delta.
04:05 Ethan Li: Sounds good. Any specific numbers we should expect baseline?
04:10 Miguel Ortega: Depends on model size and quantization. For a 7B open model on optimized runtime you might see first-token p95 around 120-300ms at low concurrency; tokens/sec for generation can be 300-800 tokens/sec on a single GPU depending on sequence length and sampling. For larger models or private infra without the optimized kernel selection we might be at 50-200 tokens/sec.
04:44 Dr. Priya Rao: Hmm, 120ms sounds optimistic — are those measured on Redwood hosted infra?
04:49 Miguel Ortega: Yes those are Redwood Hosted numbers with our optimized kernels and batching. Dedicated with reserved pools typically matches or slightly improves p95 because of isolation; Private depends on customer hardware and network.
05:00 Sofia Martinez: Regarding private: If we run in our VPC with a peered subnet, what additional latency should we account for?
05:07 Miguel Ortega: Typical VPC peering adds ~10-40ms depending on region and cross-AZ hops. If you run an on-prem install with router/firewall checks and HSM/KMS calls, that can add another 20-80ms occasionally. We'll measure that in the private pilot.
05:30 Laura Chen: Quick check — what's your SLA need? Do you need a contractual p95?
05:35 Dr. Priya Rao: For production we want SLO of p95 < 400ms for first token during normal ops; during major incidents we'll accept higher. For pilot we want a reproducible benchmark showing we can meet 350ms p95 on average.
05:51 Miguel Ortega: That's doable to validate. We'll scope the pilot to show p95 for first token and sustained throughput. We'll also test cold-start/cold-KV cache cases because clinical data varies.
06:06 Ethan Li: For streaming semantics, do you support chunked responses with partial JSON or do you expect the client to parse tokens? We need deterministic markers.
06:15 Miguel Ortega: We support streaming as token deltas; in addition you can bind structured tokens (function-like outputs) but for this case we'll stream tokens and you can parse partial summaries. We'll include a small SDK snippet in the benchmark harness so you can simulate your frontend parsing logic.
06:35 Dr. Priya Rao: How do you handle fallbacks? If dedicated pool saturates, can requests be routed to hosted or to a smaller model automatically?
06:43 Laura Chen: Yes — smart routing policies can failover to a compatible model variant or to hosted capacity depending on your policy. That tradeoff is between cost and fidelity.
06:55 Sofia Martinez: Encryption at rest — do you use customer-managed keys?
07:00 Laura Chen: Yes for Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for CMEK; Hosted supports envelope encryption with KMS and we can contract for Bring Your Own Key in enterprise plans.
07:12 Ethan Li: For the benchmark, can you simulate our auth flow? We use short-lived signed tokens via our IdP.
07:18 Miguel Ortega: We can simulate the auth headers and also run tests from your VPC for private so the handshake path is accurate.
07:25 Dr. Priya Rao: Who will own the bench infra? Redwood or us?
07:29 Miguel Ortega: For hosted and dedicated proofs we'll run from Redwood's test harness against your sample data. For private we'll run together — Redwood can ship a small harness or you can run the tests and return logs. We'll make both options available.
07:46 Laura Chen: Ok let's lock next steps — Miguel will run the microbench and realistic replay with your provided prompts, Laura will send the security packet and pricing, and Sofia will share compliance items.
07:58 Dr. Priya Rao: One practical question: we have burst windows where concurrency jumps 3x — can Redwood autoscale quickly enough without overshoot?
08:09 Miguel Ortega: Dedicated autoscaling can be tuned with burst capacity and buffer headroom; scaling is seconds-to-minutes depending on the exact instance type. For true real-time bursts we recommend provisioning a small burst pool or routing lower-priority traffic to a cheaper model variant. We'll include recommended autoscale parameters in our follow-up.
08:33 Ethan Li: Can you also show us the per-token cost delta when you enable KV cache for repeated prefixes?
08:40 Miguel Ortega: Absolutely — KV/prefix caching often reduces tokens generated per request and also reduces compute, showing big savings for repeated context patterns. We'll measure with caching on/off.
08:52 Sofia Martinez: We'll need an internal runbook for incident response if the inference pool degrades; can Redwood provide runbook templates?
08:58 Laura Chen: Yes, we have runbook templates and playbooks for failover to hosted, throttling, and circuit-breaker behaviors. We'll include that in the packet.
09:12 Dr. Priya Rao: One reminder — any PII in the sample prompts will need to be handled per our DPA; we will send anonymized prompts but may need to redact more if requested.
09:23 Laura Chen: Understood — we'll accept anonymized prompts and can sign a DPA if needed.
09:30 Miguel Ortega: Quick technical note about benchmarking methodology: we'll capture p50/p90/p95/p99 for first token and last token, measure tokens/sec, measure tail under GC/kv eviction scenarios, and report per-route latency breakdown. We'll also attach raw CSVs so you can reproduce.
09:55 Ethan Li: Great. On timeframe — can you deliver initial microbench results by Friday?
10:00 Miguel Ortega: Yes, we'll target 2025-07-18 for initial results.
10:06 Dr. Priya Rao: OK thanks everyone.
10:10 Laura Chen: Recap: send security docs, run benchmarks, schedule pilot kickoff. Thanks all.
